ownerDecisions.decision: W02d defines the WORKER allowlist from the worker's duties; the W01 section 5.3 WORKER row text 'Existing worker allowlist' is amended to 'the W02d worker allowlist' (carried to W01's record)

exact duty syscalls per role from its row plus one closed runtime base per role (CPython 3.12 for SERVER and WORKER, one native static base for the five native roles); W03's language and libc must fit inside it or W02d reopens

seccompFilterDigest is the SHA-256 of the classic-BPF sock_filter array (little-endian) the reference compiler emits per role and architecture; the boot-time proof that the installed filter equals it is an open T04/W02a-F obligation
the broker kills the worker through cgroup.kill only (it has no CAP_KILL); W6 becomes freeze, cgroup.kill, wait for populated 0, and the unused pidfd_send_signal grant is dropped
the broker runs with no supplementary groups and W3 checks the child holds none; no role may grant setgroups

M-a: memfd_create flags are MFD_CLOEXEC | MFD_NOEXEC_SEAL, so the kernel clears exec and sets F_SEAL_EXEC on every call with no reliance on host state (not a vm.memfd_noexec pin, which a CAP_SYS_ADMIN holder in the initial namespaces can lower)

NATIVE_STATIC adds three narrow rules for the Rust+musl steady state: mremap only with flags == MREMAP_MAYMOVE (musl mallocng realloc of large chunks), prctl only with arg0 == PR_SET_NAME (std and tokio thread names), and tkill (musl abort and raise); setresuid/setresgid threaded signalling, available_parallelism file reads and units starting roles with fds 0-2 open are W03 trace items

the native roles are Rust with musl, fully static (analysed reference: musl 1.2.5, Rust 1.90.0; W03 pins these or re-checks against W02d); NATIVE_STATIC adds poll, which Rust std calls on fds 0-2 at start-up and musl issues as SYS_poll on x86_64 (aarch64 has no poll syscall); musl creates threads with clone, never clone3, so the clone3 ENOSYS rule serves the CPython roles' glibc
